# # Map customer FastAPI request-body field-drop to the Pydantic v2 model_validator chain integration boundary

A customer reports that after upgrading from Pydantic v1 to Pydantic v2
their FastAPI POST endpoint silently drops a discriminated-union field on
the request body. The endpoint returns 200 OK, the response body shows the
field as None, but the client clearly sent it. No 422 error is raised.

Your task:
1. Find where FastAPI builds a request-body parameter from a Pydantic
   model and validates it before invoking the route handler.
2. Find where Pydantic v2 evaluates a discriminated union and how
   model_validator(mode='before') interacts with discriminator field
   resolution.
3. Trace the cross-repo flow: FastAPI dependency injection -> body
   parameter solving -> Pydantic model_validate_json -> discriminator
   resolution -> field assignment. Cite each file and function.
4. Identify why a model_validator(mode='before') that pre-processes
   incoming JSON can silently strip the discriminator key, leading to
   the union resolving to its default variant with the field set to None.


Search only these repositories: github.com/sg-evals/fastapi--0.110.0, github.com/sg-evals/pydantic--v2.6.4

Here is the full end-to-end trace, with the exact integration boundary where the silent drop occurs.

---

## 1. FastAPI Request-Body Construction and Validation

### Route registration and body field discovery

[`fastapi/routing.py` `APIRoute.__init__`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/fastapi--0.110.0/-/blob/fastapi/routing.py?L500-L526) calls `get_dependant()` then `get_body_field()`. The `analyze_param()` function in [`fastapi/dependencies/utils.py`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/fastapi--0.110.0/-/blob/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py?L317-L451) inspects every route-handler parameter; non-scalar Pydantic-model annotations are classified as `params.Body` and stored in `dependant.body_params` as `ModelField` instances.

For the Pydantic v2 path, `ModelField` is defined in [`fastapi/_compat.py` L83-L161](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/fastapi--0.110.0/-/blob/fastapi/_compat.py?L83-L161). On construction it immediately builds a `TypeAdapter`:

```python
# fastapi/_compat.py  L107-L109
def __post_init__(self) -> None:
    self._type_adapter: TypeAdapter[Any] = TypeAdapter(
        Annotated[self.field_info.annotation, self.field_info]
    )
```

This is where Pydantic v2's full schema — including the discriminated-union and any `model_validator` decorators — is compiled and frozen at startup time.

### Request handling

[`get_request_handler()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/fastapi--0.110.0/-/blob/fastapi/routing.py?L196-L244) reads the raw bytes and parses JSON with `await request.json()`, producing a plain Python dict, then passes it to `solve_dependencies()`.

### Dependency solving and body validation

[`solve_dependencies()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/fastapi--0.110.0/-/blob/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py?L622-L630) calls `request_body_to_args()`. Inside [`request_body_to_args()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/fastapi--0.110.0/-/blob/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py?L685-L764) the critical line is:

```python
# dependencies/utils.py  L756
v_, errors_ = field.validate(value, values, loc=loc)
```

### ModelField.validate delegates to TypeAdapter

[`ModelField.validate()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/fastapi--0.110.0/-/blob/fastapi/_compat.py?L116-L131) calls:

```python
# _compat.py  L124-L126
return (
    self._type_adapter.validate_python(value, from_attributes=True),
    None,
)
```

Any `ValidationError` is caught and re-raised as FastAPI validation errors. But if validation **succeeds** (even with wrong data), no error propagates — this is the silent path.

---

## 2. Pydantic v2 Schema Construction for Discriminated Unions

### Schema generation order

In [`_generate_schema.py` `_model_schema()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/pydantic--v2.6.4/-/blob/pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py?L504-L591), schema construction follows this sequence:

```python
# _generate_schema.py  L562-L575
fields_schema = core_schema.model_fields_schema(...)       # 1. field schemas
inner_schema = apply_validators(fields_schema, ...)         # 2. root validators
inner_schema = apply_model_validators(inner_schema, model_validators, 'inner')  # 3. BEFORE validators
model_schema = core_schema.model_schema(cls, inner_schema, ...)
schema = apply_model_validators(schema, model_validators, 'outer')  # 4. AFTER/WRAP validators
```

### `apply_model_validators` and `mode='before'`

[`apply_model_validators()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/pydantic--v2.6.4/-/blob/pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py?L2018-L2062) wraps the `inner_schema` (i.e., the `model_fields_schema`) with a `before_validator_function` when `mode == 'inner'`:

```python
# _generate_schema.py  L2049-L2053
elif validator.info.mode == 'before':
    if info_arg:
        schema = core_schema.with_info_before_validator_function(function=validator.func, schema=schema)
    else:
        schema = core_schema.no_info_before_validator_function(function=validator.func, schema=schema)
```

This means the compiled CoreSchema is: `before_validator_fn( model_fields_schema(...) )`. The `before` validator **wraps the entire fields schema**, so it runs before individual field parsing.

### Discriminator is applied at the outer Union level, not the model level

When a field on the **containing** model is declared as `Union[VariantA, VariantB] = Field(discriminator="type")`, the discriminator is applied in [`_generate_schema.py` `_apply_discriminator_to_union()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/pydantic--v2.6.4/-/blob/pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py?L403-L419), which calls [`apply_discriminator()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/pydantic--v2.6.4/-/blob/pydantic/_internal/_discriminated_union.py?L59-L95), which builds a `tagged-union` CoreSchema via [`_ApplyInferredDiscriminator.apply()`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/pydantic--v2.6.4/-/blob/pydantic/_internal/_discriminated_union.py?L165-L254):

```python
# _discriminated_union.py  L243-L254
return core_schema.tagged_union_schema(
    choices=self._tagged_union_choices,
    discriminator=discriminator,
    ...
)
```

The `tagged-union` schema is a **pydantic-core** construct: it first reads the discriminator key from the raw input, selects the matching CoreSchema for that variant, then passes the raw input to **that variant's CoreSchema** for full validation.

---

## 3. The Integration Boundary — Where the Drop Happens

The containing model's field declaration looks like:

```python
class RequestBody(BaseModel):
    payload: Union[VariantA, VariantB] = Field(discriminator="type")
```

And `VariantA` (or `VariantB`) has:

```python
class VariantA(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["a"]
    extra_field: str

    @model_validator(mode='before')
    @classmethod
    def pre_process(cls, data):
        # customer's intent: normalise keys
        return {k.lower(): v for k, v in data.items()}
        # OR: they reconstruct the dict and forget to forward "type"
```

The compiled CoreSchema for `payload` is (inside pydantic-core):

```
tagged-union(discriminator="type")
  "a" --> before_fn( model_fields_schema(VariantA) )
  "b" --> before_fn( model_fields_schema(VariantB) )
```

**Execution order** when `validate_python` is called with `{"type": "a", "extra_field": "x"}`:

1. pydantic-core reads `data["type"]` == `"a"` at the tagged-union level.
2. pydantic-core routes to `VariantA`'s schema.
3. pydantic-core invokes the `before_fn` (the `model_validator(mode='before')`) **with the same raw dict**.
4. The `before_fn` returns a new dict — if it omits `"type"`, pydantic-core continues validating `VariantA`'s `model_fields_schema` without the discriminator key.
5. `VariantA.type` is a `Literal["a"]` field with no default, so it becomes `None` (or uses its declared default if any). No `ValidationError` is raised because the **union branch was already selected at step 1** — there is nothing left to re-check the discriminator against.

---

## 4. Why No 422 Is Raised

The key insight is that **discriminator resolution and field validation are two separate pydantic-core passes**:

- **Pass 1 (tagged-union level):** pydantic-core reads the discriminator key from the *original* raw dict to select the branch. This succeeds because the client sent `"type": "a"`.
- **Pass 2 (within the chosen branch):** pydantic-core calls the `before` validator, which transforms the dict. The `before` validator's return value is what gets field-validated. If `"type"` is absent from the returned dict, the `Literal["a"]` field receives no input.

Because `Literal["a"]` has no `default=`, pydantic **would** normally raise a `missing` error — **unless** the model declares `model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)` with a default, or the field has `Optional` wrapping, or the customer's `before` validator returns a value but strips the key from an `Optional[Literal["a"]] = None` field. In practice, customers often write `type: Optional[Literal["a"]] = None` as a convenience, making the missing key silently coerce to `None` with no error. The result is:

- No `422` (pydantic-core never re-evaluates discriminator correctness after the `before` validator runs).
- No branch mismatch error (the union branch was already committed).
- `field = None` in the response body.

| 3. Field.validate | [`utils.py:756`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/fastapi--0.110.0/-/blob/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py?L756) | `request_body_to_args` | `field.validate(value, ...)` |
| 4. TypeAdapter | [`_compat.py:124-126`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/fastapi--0.110.0/-/blob/fastapi/_compat.py?L124-L126) | `ModelField.validate` | `TypeAdapter.validate_python(value, from_attributes=True)` |
| 5. Discriminator read | [`_discriminated_union.py:243-254`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/pydantic--v2.6.4/-/blob/pydantic/_internal/_discriminated_union.py?L243-L254) | `_ApplyInferredDiscriminator._apply_to_root` | tagged-union reads `data["type"]`, selects variant |
| 6. `before` validator | [`_generate_schema.py:2049-2053`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/pydantic--v2.6.4/-/blob/pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py?L2049-L2053) | `apply_model_validators` (mode='inner') | `model_validator(mode='before')` transforms the dict, may strip `"type"` |
| **7. Silent drop** | pydantic-core (Rust) | `tagged_union_schema` executor | Branch already committed; missing `"type"` sets field to `None` with no error |
| 8. 200 returned | [`routing.py:277-307`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/fastapi--0.110.0/-/blob/fastapi/routing.py?L277-L307) | `get_request_handler / app()` | `errors=[]`, response serialized normally |

### Fix

The `model_validator(mode='before')` must **preserve the discriminator key** in its return value:

```python
@model_validator(mode='before')
@classmethod
def pre_process(cls, data: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(data, dict):
        result = {k.lower(): v for k, v in data.items()}
        # Ensure the discriminator key is forwarded
        # (it was already used to reach this branch, but must survive for field assignment)
        return result
    return data
```

Or, declare the discriminator field non-optional with no default so pydantic raises `missing` instead of silently using `None`:

```python
type: Literal["a"]   # not Optional, no default
```
